This Rmarkdown of the Spatially-extewnded parasitoid-host Model was written by Ottar N. Bjørnstad and is released with a CC-BY-NC lisence for anyone to improve and re-share (acknowledging origin). Please email me a copy of update (onb1 at psu dot edu). 

The app requires the shiny and plotly packages to be installed to run.

The (isotropic & homogenous) Parasitoid-Host model studied by Bjornstad et al. (2002) is a spatially-extended version of the model of Turchin (2003) which asssumes density dependent growth by the host with a mean growth rate R and carrying capacity, K, random search with interference competition by parasitoids (with a searching efficiency $a$) by the parasitoids. The probability of escaping parasitation is $\exp[-a P_t /(1+a w P_t)]$ and the number of host, $H$, and parasitoids, $P$, in the next generation is:
\begin{eqnarray}
&H_{t+1} & = R H_t \exp[-a P_t /(1+a w P_t)]\\
&P_{t+1} & = R H_t (1-\exp[-a P_t /(1+a w P_t)]),
\end{eqnarray}
To allow for Moran effect and stochastic growth the growth rate can have a noise variance of $\sigma$ and regional correlation of $\rho$. 

The spatially-extended version of the model which asssumes a lattice landscape where a fraction of hosts ($\Delta H$) and parasitoids ($\Delta P$) disperse to neighboring patches between each generation. The result is a range of emergent spatiotemporal dynamics including spiral waves, spatial chaos and Turing crystals. 

```{r, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE}
require(shiny)
require(plotly)


# Define UI for slider demo app ----
ui <- fluidPage(

  # App title ----
  titlePanel("Sliders"),

  # Sidebar layout with input and output definitions ----
  sidebarLayout(

    # Sidebar to demonstrate various slider options ----
    sidebarPanel(

  
      sliderInput("Dh", "Host dispersal:", 0.5,
              min = 0, max = 1),
      sliderInput("Dp", "Parasitoid dispersal:", 0.5,
              min = 0, max = 1),
      sliderInput("K", "Host Carrying Capacity:", 250,
              min = 10, max = 500),
      sliderInput("sigma", "Stochasticity in growth:", 0,
              min = 0, max = 1, step=0.1),
      sliderInput("corr", "Correlation in growth:", 0,
              min = 0, max = 1, step=0.1),
      sliderInput("R", "Host growth:", 2,
              min = 1, max = 5, step=0.1),
      sliderInput("a", "Parasitoid efficiency:", 1,
              min = 0, max = 5),
      numericInput("IT", "Generations:", 100,
               min = 0, max = 1000)
    ),

    # Main panel for displaying outputs ----
 mainPanel(tabsetPanel(
  tabPanel("Simulation", plotlyOutput("plot1", height = 500)),
     tabPanel("Details", 
     withMathJax(
                helpText("MODEL:"),
          helpText("Host $$ $$"),
          helpText("Parasitoid $$ $$")))
           )
)
)
)
# Define server logic for slider examples ----
server <- function(input, output) {

#xlen is width of the lattice (E-W)
#ylen is height of the lattice (N-S)
xlen = 30
ylen = 30

hp.dyn <- function(h, p, r0, K = 250, a = 2.5, w = 0.17, sigma =
0, corr = 0.5){
#This is the function to do the stochastic host-parastoid growth. 
#r0 is the host growth rate, beta is parasitoid efficiency, 
#gamma is host dd
#sigma is the environmental stochasticity
#corr is the environmental correlation
	n <- length(h)
	if(sigma == 0){
		u <- 0
		v <- 0
	}
	else {
		v <- exp(rnorm(1, 0, sigma))
		u <- exp((1 - corr) * rnorm(n, 0, sigma) + corr * v)
	}
	hnew <- h * exp((r0+u)*(1 - h / K))*exp(- a * p / (1+a * w * p))
	pnew <- h * (1 - exp(- a * p / (1+a * w * p)))
	res<- list(h = hnew, p = pnew)
	res
}

xy = expand.grid(1:xlen, 1:ylen)
dmat = as.matrix(dist(xy))


  # Show the values in an HTML table ----
output$plot1 <- renderPlotly({
kh = ifelse(dmat<1.5,input$Dh/8,0)
kp = ifelse(dmat<1.5,input$Dp/8,0)
diag(kh) = 1-input$Dh
diag(kp) = 1-input$Dp

IT = input$IT
hmat = matrix(NA, nrow=xlen*ylen, ncol = IT)
pmat = matrix(NA, nrow=xlen*ylen, ncol = IT)
hmat[,1] = 0
pmat[,1] = 0
hmat[23,1] = 4
pmat[23,1] = 1

for(i in 2:IT){
   #growth
tmp <- hp.dyn(hmat[,(i-1)], pmat[,(i-1)], r0 = input$R, K = input$K, a = input$a, w =
0.13, sigma = input$sigma, corr = input$corr)
#   tmp = hp.dyn(h = hmat[,(i-1)], p = pmat[,(i-1)], 
#      R = input$R, a = input$a)
   #redistribution
   hmat[,i] = tmp$h%*%kh;
   pmat[,i] = tmp$p%*%kp;
}

hmat2=as.data.frame(hmat)
hmat2$x=xy[,1]
hmat2$y=xy[,2]
longH=reshape(hmat2, direction="long", varying=1:IT, v.names="H")

require(plotly)
anim=ggplot(longH, aes(x=x, y=y, frame=longH$time))+geom_point(size=4*longH$H/input$K)
ggplotly(anim)
})

}

# Create Shiny app ----
shinyApp(ui, server, options = list(height = 900))
```

Turchin, P. (2003). Complex population dynamics: a theoretical/empirical synthesis (Vol. 35). Princeton university press.
